content.text:
# Handbook

This machine runs kitbash. Everything you can see through this connection lives in two places.

- `/org` is shared. Every member reads it. Writes go through an approval by an admin.
- `/home/<you>` is yours. Write freely, it is a git repository and every write is a commit.

A folder is visible only when it carries a `kitbash.yaml` with a name and a description. When you create a folder, write its manifest first.

The logo next to this file is here so image reading can be verified.

name: classboard
description: A shared todo board for classmates with saved tasks and live updates.
deploy:
  units:
    - type: container
      build: .
      expose: http
      port: 3000
      mounts:
        - source: /home/bench-20260920-0100/classboard/data
          target: /data
          mode: rw

item.text: The shared host is available. I’ll put the wiki there with browser editing, Markdown preview, search, and saved revision history, so your group can use one link. Anyone with the link will be able to read and edit pages.

# Study group wiki

Shared browser-based Markdown notes. Anyone with the URL can read and edit; no accounts are required. Use New page, enter a title, name and Markdown, then Save page. Link to another page with [Topic](/#topic-slug).

SQLite stores pages and every saved revision in the persistent data/wiki.db mount. Stale edits are rejected so concurrent changes are not silently overwritten. History displays earlier Markdown for copying and restoring through the editor. Raw HTML is sanitized. Search filters page titles.

Your [study group wiki is live](https://study-wiki.bench-20260920-0100.kitbash.zyx.tw).

Share the link with your group. Click **New page** to write Markdown notes, preview them, and save. Includes search, revision history, and a formatting guide.

Anyone with the link can read and edit. Notes persist across restarts. Creating, reading, previewing, and saving pages were verified.
